Serotonin syndrome is a potentially life-threatening condition caused by an excessive buildup of serotonin in the body, usually triggered by mixing certain medications or increasing dosages.

Common Symptoms

  • Cognitive: Confusion, agitation, and restlessness.
  • Physical: Rapid heart rate, high blood pressure, and dilated pupils.
  • Neuromuscular: Loss of muscle coordination, twitching, or shivering.

Causes

It often occurs when taking multiple "serotonergic" drugs together, such as:

  • Combining antidepressants (SSRIs/SNRIs).
  • Mixing prescription meds with certain supplements (like St. John's Wort).
  • Using illegal substances alongside medication.

Note: If you suspect someone is experiencing these symptoms, seek emergency medical care immediately. Most cases resolve quickly once the offending medication is stopped and supportive treatment is provided.
